correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact normalized weighted Dirichlet space, strict parameters -1<alpha<0, a,b in (0,1), and Fredholm/Calkin essential spectrum. The codimension-one derivative model identifies each C_{phi_a} modulo finite rank with D_a=a C_{phi_a} on weighted Bergman A^2_alpha. The Cayley+Bergman unitary followed by the Paley-Wiener weighted Laplace realization gives D_a exactly as a^(-alpha/2) M_{exp(-(1-a)t)} U_a on L²((0,infinity),t^(-alpha-1)dt), where U_s f(t)=s^(-alpha/2) f(st) is unitary. Direct multiplication and adjoints yield K=(ab)^(-alpha/2) M_{exp(-c1*t)-exp(-c2*t)} U_{a/b}, c1=1-a+a(1-b)/b>0 and c2=(2-a-b)/b>c1 with gap 2(1-a)(1-b)/b. For the nonatomic L² space, multiplication has essential norm its essential supremum; the positive multiplier maximizes at t*=log(c2/c1)/(c2-c1), giving exactly (ab)^(-alpha/2)(1-theta)theta^(theta/(1-theta)). When a=b, the dilation is I and the Calkin spectral range is [0,norm]. When a/b=r!=1, the weight satisfies h(t)<=B min(t,t^-1), and for every n and t=r^u, the product of n orbit weights is <=B^n q^(-sum_{k=0}^{n-1}|u+k|)<=B^n q^(-floor(n²/4)) (q=max(r,1/r)>1). Spectral radius is zero, while essential norm is positive; no finite experiment is used as proof. Endpoint exclusions and diagonal theta=a were checked.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Spectral descriptions of an individual composition operator or separate ordered products cannot determine the spectrum of their noncommutative difference. For a/b!=1, h(t) vanishes at both multiplicative ends; the orbit crosses these ends and yields superexponential power decay. In the diagonal case U_1=I and the multiplier essential range is an interval. This exact paired spectrum is not stated or directly implied by the inspected broader operator classifications. A sufficiently general weighted composition operator theorem might streamline the last step but would not automatically identify the explicit Dirichlet commutator model.

In the Laplace model the weight is a difference of exponentials, not the single positive exponential of a composition operator. The exact supremum and quasinilpotence are not logical consequences of compactness alone.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge originality of the exact singular-weight cross-adjoint commutator essential norm and the Calkin spectral dichotomy. The closest published analyses establish only compactness of cross-adjoint commutators, or essential-norm estimates for the two separate ordered products, or spectra of individual composition operators. Importantly, the classical derivative model makes the weighted Bergman compactness theorems directly relevant: the known theorem already implies this family is noncompact, so noncompactness alone is not credited as new. None of the materially inspected primary results gives the exact difference norm or the off-diagonal nonzero quasinilpotent Calkin class. The reduction to an explicit difference-of-exponentials weighted dilation and its superexponential orbit-product bound are the surviving content. The 2012 historical commutator paper could not be read in full; its abstract/successor establish qualitative compactness, and any uninspected quantitative statements remain a recorded priority risk.

value.rationale: The 2026 weighted-Dirichlet product literature has sharp essential norm results outside the singular range but only comparability bounds for the individual product orders for -1<alpha<0. The same two-parameter affine boundary-contact family yields a natural commutator testing essential commutativity and essential normality. Its exact nonzero norm is a sharp quantitative invariant, and the full diagonal interval versus off-diagonal nonzero quasinilpotent Calkin element is a genuine structural phase boundary invisible from the previously known compactness classification. The mechanism (two-endpoint damping of multiplicative orbits) is mathematically motivated and general enough to inform analyses of affine adjoint products. It is a natural complete two-parameter calculation, not arbitrary low-dimensional enumeration; no general linear-fractional theorem is claimed.
